Meta Ordered to Pay $567 Million In New Mexico for Teen Mental Health Fund

A New Mexico state court ordered Meta on Thursday to pay $567 million into a teen mental health fund and change how its platforms function for young users after finding the company is to blame for harming children’s wellbeing. The ruling comes five months after a New Mexico jury in an earlier phase of the case ordered Meta to pay $375 million after finding it violated consumer protection law by misrepresenting the safety of Facebook and Instagram for young users. Biedscheid on Thursday ordered Meta to implement youth-safety measures, including monthly limits on teens’ use of Facebook and Instagram, restrictions on notifications, tighter controls on adult contact with minors, safeguards for AI chatbots, and enhanced review of child sexual abuse reports, under a decree that will be in place for five years.

TSR lowers hurricane season forecast as sub-tropical Atlantic looking less favourable

Tropical Storm Risk (TSR) has now lowered its forecast for the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season at an update today, citing “conditions in the sub-tropical Atlantic looking less favourable than as appeared to be a month ago.” Recall that, in its April forecast, Tropical Storm Risk (TSR) lowered its previous long-range forecast to call for 12 named tropical storms, 5 hurricanes and just 1 major hurricane for the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season, with expected accumulated cyclone energy (ACE) of 66. TSR has lowered its forecast from early July due to conditions in the sub-tropical Atlantic looking less favourable than as appeared to be a month ago.” On the ACE Index, TSR now says it sees a 0% probability of the 2026 season being in the upper tercile (>156)), a 26% likelihood of being in the middle tercile (75 to 156)) and a 74% chance of being lower tercile with ACE below 75. But, with the season passing and approaching its accepted peak, TSR now feels tropical conditions are less conducive to storm formation again, reducing the figures in today’s forecast update for the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season.

Climate Change Made ‘Fire Weather’ in France, Spain More Likely

Climate change made the weather that fueled Europe’s recent wildfires at least twice as likely in France and at least 20 times as likely in Spain, scientists at the World Weather Attribution group said on Friday. In today’s climate, the weather underlying such intense wildfires can be expected to occur every 20 years in southwestern France and every six years in central Spain, the study found, based on a comparison of historical summer conditions to this year’s.
